record.paper_title: The 1999 Heineman Prize Address Integrable models in statistical mechanics: The hidden field with unsolved problems
record.original_question: Can one explicitly reconstruct the meromorphic function required in Baxter's chiral-Potts order-parameter approach from its known zeros and poles on the relevant Riemann surface, thereby resolving the algebraic-geometric obstruction that currently blocks the higher-genus solution?

evidence.quote: In another approach [45] a major step in the solution involves the explicit reconstruction of a meromorphic function from a knowledge of its zeros and poles. This is a classic problem in algebraic geometry for which in fact no explicit answer is known either.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the framework arising in Baxter's approach to computing the order parameter (spontaneous magnetization) of the N-state chiral Potts model in statistical mechanics. In this approach one is led to a compact Riemann surface S (of genus greater than one, depending on N) associated with the rapidity curve of the model, together with a prescribed divisor D = ∑ n_i P_i − ∑ m_j Q_j on S, where the points P_i, Q_j ∈ S and the positive integer multiplicities n_i, m_j (the orders of the prescribed zeros and poles) are explicitly known.

The Riemann–Roch theorem guarantees, for a divisor of sufficiently high degree, the existence of a meromorphic function f on S whose divisor of zeros and poles equals D. The problem is to give an explicit construction of such a meromorphic function f on S in closed form (for instance, as an explicit combination of theta functions, abelian integrals, or other classical transcendental objects intrinsically attached to S), starting from the data of the prescribed zeros, poles, and their multiplicities.

Equivalently: provide an explicit, computable formula realizing the existence statement of Abel's theorem / Riemann–Roch for the higher-genus Riemann surfaces arising in the chiral Potts model, thereby removing the algebraic-geometric obstruction to carrying out the higher-genus version of the order-parameter calculation along these lines.
artifact.category_tag: Chiral Potts model / meromorphic functions on Riemann surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The order parameter of the chiral Potts model itself was proved by Baxter in 2005, but via a different (functional-equation / "broken rapidity line") route based on an analyticity assumption, rather than by explicitly constructing the required meromorphic function on the higher-genus Riemann surface from its zeros and poles. The underlying algebraic-geometric problem of writing such a meromorphic function in explicit closed form on the relevant high-genus chiral-Potts Riemann surface does not appear to have an explicit general solution in the literature; thus while the physics problem motivating it is now resolved, the explicit reconstruction question asked here remains essentially open / bypassed.

status_evidence.title: The Order Parameter of the Chiral Potts Model
status_evidence.snippet: Baxter proves the order-parameter conjecture under an analyticity assumption using the broken-rapidity-line method, not by explicit meromorphic reconstruction.
status_evidence.claim: The chiral Potts order parameter conjecture was proved in 2005 by an alternative method.

status_evidence.title: Derivation of the order parameter of the chiral Potts model
status_evidence.snippet: Companion derivation by Baxter (2005) using functional relations rather than the explicit Riemann-surface reconstruction program.
status_evidence.claim: The 2005 derivation circumvents the explicit higher-genus meromorphic reconstruction.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Potts model - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: States that the order-parameter conjecture was proved by Baxter in 2005 using the broken rapidity line technique of Jimbo et al.
status_evidence.claim: Resolution of the order parameter problem did not proceed via explicit zero/pole reconstruction.
